title: Restore a robot vacuum whose main brush was misseated after cleaning
justification: Direct service of an actual autonomous floor-cleaning robot; the drive must engage and the retaining cover must physically close before the robot can resume work.
fault: The main rubber brush has its drive end resting proud of the keyed socket after a failed reinstall. The opposite bearing is in its open pocket. The free cover rests beside the upside-down powered-off robot.
instruction: Restore the robot vacuum’s main brush and cover so it is ready to clean.
objects: Full-scale Roborock S7 chassis, 353 x 350 x 96.5 mm, approximately 4.7 kg, inverted and powered off
S7 rubber main roller with helical vanes, drive key and removable bearing end
Real removable cover: rear hooks and two spring catches at opposite edge; not a hinged door
SimReady mug and tape as irrelevant workbench objects
skill: Extract a canted roller, align its drive end into a recessed keyed socket, lower its bearing into its pocket, hook the separate cover under the chassis edge and engage its catches. Physical contacts must prevent a closed cover over a proud roller. Any safe one-handed alternative remains valid.
scoring: Proposed 0.5 only for roller actually driven by socket and both bearing shoulders seated; 1.0 additionally cover hooks and both catches physically retained, released/still 1s. Falls or damage override all credit. Numeric tolerances to be set from source-reconstructed geometry before demo tuning.

nearest.comparison: Same broad brush-service job but rejected for bare fixture, bristleless cylinder, and software-only catch. Not held; current proposal must fix these central fidelity omissions, not merely change colors.
Only brush-door opening, rejected importance because task stops before maintenance. Current task restores roller drive and retained assembly.
Lift vacuum off a trapped remote and press start; inspected full task.json. Distinct whole-unit obstacle removal with no brush servicing.
Manual robot tool changer; tool seating plus cam locking. Different functional brush-bearing assembly but keyed insertion overlap remains a reviewer risk.

risks: Main roller subpart dimensions are not in public user manual; must obtain sufficiently grounded part geometry before tuning.

No SimReady robot vacuum in catalogue: full source-reconstructed chassis and task-critical mechanism needed, explicitly disclosed, with SimReady distractors. Parent authorized grounded full-unit direction.
A simple loose-cylinder placement with pose-triggered software latch would repeat2169 and is prohibited.
No invented threaded hair wad or forced bimanual rule to manufacture difficulty.
Safe remove-and-reinstall remains valid; distinct skill is real recessed drive engagement plus free cover hooks/catches, not a pose mark.

primary_hardware_comparison.inspected: Downloaded PDF and viewed pages27-28 (PDF pages25-26), showing brush, bearing, twist caps, and separate two-catch cover.
primary_hardware_comparison.cover: Official product photographs confirm four fixed rear hooks and two inward-sliding spring catches. Full free cover model, no permanent hinge.
primary_hardware_comparison.scale: Manufacturer overall size353x350x96.5 mm; subpart geometry pending product photographs or CAD.
primary_hardware_comparison.no_accommodation: No grip tabs, widened end socket, hidden fixed chassis fixture, or hand-count requirements. Chassis remains free with actual mass.

strict_review.importance: Pass provisionally: direct functional robot servicing, unlike printer maintenance indirectly connected to robot parts.2169 had construct/clarity rejection, not importance.
strict_review.construct: Conditional: must ground the keyed drive, pocket and actual cover catch geometry; build only if supported.
strict_review.novelty: Conditional pending2033 file check; no accepted/pending brush install in fresh2411PR snapshot.2169 and2103 are final-closed.
strict_review.shortcut: Allow ordinary safe removal/reinstall. Do not claim interlock recovery if simply lowering an aligned cylinder earns full credit.
strict_review.verdict: Proceed to source geometry and contact prototype; no validated count yet.

live_comparison_2033.state: OPEN, latest revision TK-UYHAKY waiting review
live_comparison_2033.evidence: Read actual PR diff including README, setup, scoring and demo. It lifts a 34cm vacuum off a trapped remote, extracts remote, sets chassis flat and presses start. No brush drive, brush removal/insertion or cover retention.
live_comparison_2033.distinction: Brush servicing requires physically engaging recessed keyed motor drive, seating bearing and retaining separate cover with hooks/catches; safe remove/reinstall preserves these skills. It is not trapped-object removal or start-button recovery.
live_comparison_2033.remaining: Full contact feasibility, dimensional provenance and final accepted/pending comparison remain required.
